rows.title_full: AN ACT EXCLUDING THE OFFICIAL DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE (ODA) FROM THE FOREIGN DEBT LIMIT IN ORDER TO FACILITATE THE ABSORPTION AND OPTIMIZE THE UTILIZATION OF ODA RESOURCES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PARRAGRAPH 1, SECTION 2 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4860
rows.abstract: "Official Development Assistance Act of 1996" Seeks to address the economic opportunities available to the country, the country's increasing economic needs and investments which require adequate financial funding and infrastructure support. The seeks to EXCLUDE the highly concessional OFFICIAL DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE or ODA loans from the foreign borrowing limit of $10 BILLION. ODA loans have the following advantages: (1)  They provide CHEAPER sources of funds than commercial loans; (2) They have a longer maturity period and cheaper interest rates -- they exert LESS pressure on the coutnry's foreign exchange reserves; (3) They promote stability in domestic interest rates.  The government does not need to compete with local private borrowerss or scarce financial resources.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COMMISSION ON THE SETTLEMENT OF LAND PROBLEMS AND TRANSFERRING IT TO THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 561 AND EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292
rows.abstract: Declares that the COMMISSION ON THE SETTLEMENT OF LAND PROBLEMS (COSLAP) shall have ORIGINAL jurisdiction to decide the following cases: (1) PETITIONS FOR THE CANCELLATION OF LAND TITLES OBTAINED EITHER BY JUDICIAL OR ADMINISTRATIVE PROCEEDINGS THROUGH FRAUD, DECEIT, MISTAKE, OVERSIGHT OR ACQUIRED THROUGH OTHER ILLEGAL, ERRONEOUS AND CORRUPT PRACTICES; (2) PETITIONS FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF BOUNDARY DISPUTES BETWEEN BARANGAYS, MUNICIPALITIES, CITIES AND PROVINCES; (3) CASES INVOLVING OWNERSHIP ORPOSSESSIONS OF PRIVATE LANDS NOT COVERED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO.6657 AND RELATED LAWS BETWEEN LANDOWNERS AND OCCUPANTS OR SQUATTERS; (4) CASES FOR CORRECTION OF ERRONEOUSLY APPROVED PRIVATE OR CADASTRAL SURVEYS; (5) LAND REGISTRATION CASES; AND (6) LANDPROBLEMS OR DISPUTES INVOLVING PUBLIC LANDS BETWEEN OCCUPANTS OR SQUATTERS AND AWARDEES OF LEASE AGREEMENTS, CONCESSIONS, PERMITS, LICENSES AND OTHER SIMILAR PRIVILEGES.

rows.abstract: Rationale: "P.D. No. 140 was enacted for the purpose of checking whether xerox and other photocopying machines are used for the production of subversive propaganda materials and in the falsification of letters and important papers and documents. Under said decree, owners or operators of said equipments are directed to register theri photocopying machines with the Philippine National Police or the National Bureau of Investigation. The repeal of P.D. No. 140 would unload the Philippine National Police of lots of paperwork, wherein time spent for this task could be better utilized to attend to more important issues and activities especially in the light of growing concern about the peace and order situation in our country.
